questions.q: What event brought Desmond Tutu and the Dalai Lama together to discuss joy?
questions.why: Tutu celebrated his 80th birthday in Dharamsala, where the Dalai Lama was based.

questions.q: Which example does the book use to show suffering is unavoidable?
questions.why: Birth is highlighted as a painful yet essential process.

questions.q: According to the authors, what is the main difference between suffering and our reaction to it?
a: We control our reaction, not the suffering
We control both suffering and reaction
Suffering is more powerful than reaction
questions.why: They emphasize mental immunity as control over reaction.

questions.q: Which feelings are suggested to replace fear and frustration caused by suffering?
questions.why: The book proposes channeling stress into compassion and sadness.

questions.q: What does the Dalai Lama and Desmond Tutu agree about fear?
a: It is a mental creation, not reality
It is a natural response to danger
It is the root of all suffering
It can be eliminated by meditation
questions.why: They state fear is a mental creation.
